references.text: The frogs were removed from Pharaoh, his house and his servants, as Moses had asked - the fulfillment of the promise in verse 7
Describes the invasion of frogs into the houses, among the servants and among the people - the same places mentioned in verse 7 where they are to disappear from
The Nile is mentioned as the place where the fish died - here in 8:7 the Nile is the place where the frogs are to remain
The psalmist recalls the plague of frogs that struck Egypt, including the king's chambers
Moses promises that the plagues will cease when he leaves the city - the same pattern with a promise that the plague will end
The locusts were cast into the Red Sea; none were left - similar removal of a plague as with the frogs
Describes the start of the plague of frogs which directly leads to the withdrawal mentioned in the source verse.
Direct narrative connection confirming the invasion of the frogs before the withdrawal.
Creates a powerful theological contrast between the Nile as a place of death and as a refuge for God's judgment creatures.
